analysis:
In the 8 November 2016 address the stated aims were to break the grip of corruption and black money, to curb fake currency used by 'enemies from across the border', and to cut terror financing. The text also said holders would have until 30 December 2016 ('50 days') to deposit old notes. At a Goa event on 13 November 2016 Modi asked for time until 30 December (press reports); the 'give me 50 days' phrasing was not found verbatim in the sources opened.

The RBI Annual Report 2017-18 (as reported) said Rs 15.31 lakh crore of Rs 15.42 lakh crore specified bank notes came back, 99.3%. The speech did not itself say how much would remain unreturned, but the policy was widely discussed as a way to extinguish unaccounted cash; the returned share leaves little unreturned value.

RBI counterfeit detections in the banking system were 7.62 lakh in 2016-17 and 5.22 lakh in 2017-18, then 2.17 lakh in 2024-25, though fake Rs 500 notes of the new design rose in 2024-25. Currency in circulation was Rs 36.87 lakh crore in March 2025. Digital payments growth and tax-base effects, which supporters cite as benefits, were not assessed here. The Supreme Court (2023, 4-1) upheld the decision-making process; it did not rule on outcomes.
notes: Verdict is a judgment on the mixed outcome of the stated goals; reviewer may prefer 'misleading' or split into separate claims per goal. Government's defence (e.g. digitisation, tax-base widening) not sourced; govt_response left empty. The 'Dec 30 / punishment' passage is from search summaries only.
